Home/IoT sensors/Custom gas sensor

Explosion-protected custom gas sensors.
Your gas.
Your installation.

The Hitelecom H Series custom gas sensor measures gas concentration at selected industrial monitoring points. Target gases include CH4, H2, NH3, O2, SF6, CO2, H2S, CO, SO2 and more. Sensing technology, range and units are matched to each target gas and monitoring task. Powered by an external 9–24 V DC supply, the terminal supports fixed or ducted installation and model-dependent wireless reporting. Select the gas channels, site protection, local warning requirements and platform integration as one project configuration.

Choose the gas.
Define the decision.

Useful gas measurements start with the hazard and the action required at each point. Specify the gas inventory, expected concentrations and site conditions, then select the sensing principle, units, range and installation with the required alarm and response behavior.

SENSING & INSTALLATION

Assess the gas path.
Make every point serviceable.

Choose candidate monitoring points from probable releases, gas dispersion, ventilation, obstructions and occupied locations. Gas density is one input; release temperature, gas mixtures and airflow can change movement. Agree the layout using the selected detector documentation and site assessment. For ducted or sampled monitoring, review the gas inlet, sample materials, condensation, flow and transport time. Plan external power and cable routing with the hazardous-area installation requirements. Keep each point accessible for function testing, calibration and replacement, then commission the complete measurement and alarm path.

FROM GAS MEASUREMENT TO SITE RESPONSE

See the gas condition.
Define the response.

Define sensing, alarm evaluation and data uploading as separate requirements. Specify how quickly the site needs to recognize a gas condition and how the receiving team will act. Confirm response time, upload timing, network-loss behavior and fault reporting with the ordered configuration. Where local warnings or protective actions are required, agree the appropriate local path and verify it during commissioning.

01

Measure

The selected sensing channel measures the target gas at a defined point. Confirm units, range, site conditions and sensing frequency for the duty.

02

Transmit

Readings follow the configured wireless route. Verify coverage, message format, timestamps and delivery to the agreed platform.

03

Respond

Agree thresholds, alarm recipients and site procedures. Confirm any required local warning or control path and its fault behavior as part of the project.

REPORTING & POWERExternal power for the configured duty.

The custom gas configuration uses external 9–24 V DC power. Plan the available supply, wiring, cable route and access for isolation and service with the selected detector. Confirm supply quality, component limits and any project continuity requirements during engineering review. Define the sensing and communication profile for the required monitoring duty, and document the power arrangement together with the installation and applicable hazardous-area conditions.

ANSWERS FOR YOUR PROJECT

Frequently asked questions.

Practical answers for choosing target gases, configuring sensing and external power, assessing installation conditions and connecting data to the required site response.

Ask about your project ↗
Which gases can be configured?+

Target gases include CH4, H2, NH3, O2, SF6, CO2, H2S, CO, SO2 and more. Share any additional target gases, expected concentrations and the purpose of the reading: combustible leak warning, toxic-gas monitoring, oxygen deficiency or enrichment, or an engineered process measurement. Hitelecom confirms the suitable sensing technology, selected channels, ranges and terminal arrangement in the proposal. Multi-gas projects are defined around the individual monitoring points and channel requirements.

Should our range use ppm, vol% or %LEL?+

Choose the units for the gas and monitoring duty. Combustible leak warning commonly uses percentage of the lower explosive limit (%LEL), toxic-gas measurements commonly use ppm, and oxygen measurement uses vol%. Methane monitoring for low-level leak investigation differs from a %LEL warning duty. Share expected concentrations and required response so the configured range, resolution and alarm basis can be confirmed for each channel.

How is the sensing principle selected for H2, O2 and other gases?+

Select the technology for the target gas and concentration duty. Conventional hydrocarbon infrared sensing does not detect hydrogen; hydrogen-capable catalytic and dedicated electrochemical approaches exist for different tasks. Oxygen needs an oxygen-specific channel, while PID detection depends on the gas and lamp and is commonly used for ionizable VOCs. Engineering reviews the exact sensor, interference, response and operating limits with the application.

Can a project monitor several gases?+

Yes, a project can be specified with the gas inventory and monitoring points your team needs. Hitelecom confirms the available sensing channels and terminal arrangement for that request. Combustible, toxic and oxygen duties may require different channels or devices. Include likely gas mixtures and cross-sensitivity concerns so the selected measurements and their alarm requirements can be reviewed as a complete project.

How do we specify a configuration for a hazardous area?+

Provide the site's hazardous-area classification and destination market with the enquiry. Match the supplied detector's applicable approval and exact configuration to the gas group, temperature and ambient conditions required at the site. Review the certificate coverage, marking, installation instructions and any conditions of use, including the power and wiring arrangement. Where IECEx documentation is applicable, verify the controlled online certificate and its current status.

How do enclosure protection and hazardous-area approval relate?+

Select the enclosure and gas inlet for dust, water, corrosion and the required gas access. The published family describes a customizable IP68 option; confirm its test conditions for the supplied assembly. An ingress protection rating addresses dust and water. Hazardous-area selection separately requires the applicable detector approval, marking and installation conditions, and any required detection-performance or functional-safety evidence is assessed for the project duty.

What power supply should we plan?+

The custom gas configuration uses external 9–24 V DC power. Include the available supply, cable route, isolation and service access in the project brief. Engineering confirms the supply requirements and wiring for the selected detector and installation, including the applicable hazardous-area conditions. Agree any continuity requirements together with the sensing, alarm and communication duties so the complete arrangement can be documented before commissioning.

How can we connect readings and remote notifications?+

The published family lists 4G, NB-IoT and LoRa variants and MQTT. For a cellular project, confirm the modem, regional network support, endpoint, authentication and payload. For LoRa, agree the gateway and server route. Set upload timing and remote threshold notifications for the operating workflow, and confirm timestamps, communication-fault handling and any required local warnings separately with the supplied configuration.

Can the system support ventilation or shutdown requirements?+

Include the required protective action in the enquiry so the interfaces and complete control design can be reviewed. Define the local detection and warning path, response time, fault behavior and test requirements. A remote threshold notification is an operational data function; a ventilation or shutdown duty needs the appropriate controller path and approval evidence. Hitelecom confirms the available interfaces and project suitability before those functions are specified.

Where should gas-monitoring points be placed?+

Choose candidate points from probable releases, gas dispersion, ventilation, obstructions and exposure locations. Gas density is one input: release temperature, gas mixtures and circulation can change the path, so a universal ceiling or floor height is unsuitable. Review the layout against the selected detector documentation and site assessment, with practical access for calibration and replacement. Where needed, use dispersion analysis or airflow checks to refine the plan.

When is fixed, ducted or sampled monitoring appropriate?+

Match the arrangement to the release source and measurement purpose. A fixed point measures gas reaching that point; a duct sample represents the sampled stream. Where tubing is used, review gas and material compatibility, adsorption, condensation, filters, flow faults and transport delay. Select and verify the complete gas path with the detector so its measurements represent the intended location and required response.

What information helps prepare the quotation and service plan?+

Provide target gases, units and ranges, point count, process and ambient conditions, area classification, external power, communication and alarm requirements. Add a site layout and likely interfering gases. Request the final channel specifications and applicable approvals, plus the calibration method, function-test schedule and replacement plan. Inspection and maintenance intervals are selected for the actual sensor and site conditions, with commissioning checks for the complete measurement and response path.
